English · 简体中文

Download Cindy  ·  Website  ·  Build with us  ·  Get help

★ GitHub Trending #1 · 2026.10.26

Cindy is an **open-source AI agent, ready out of the box and yours to shape**. Connect your computers and phone, bring the models and subscriptions you already use, and build a companion that knows how you like to work. ## All your devices. One Cindy. Your work computer, home desktop, laptop and phone belong together. - **Pick up the same work.** Open a session from another device, continue the conversation, and access its files without copying everything into a new chat. - **Share more than a screen.** Use model providers configured on another computer — including supported subscriptions, API providers and local models. - **Reach your whole desktop.** Built-in remote desktop on your phone lets you open apps, type and operate a connected computer when a chat isn't enough. Your computer becomes your server: **no server rental or self-hosting setup**.
How connections and data work For remote access to your computers, keep them online, sign in with the same account and enable the relevant permissions. Model sharing requires allowing remote access to that provider; remote desktop also needs its own permissions. Project files stay on their computer — remote access is not whole-disk sync. Cloud companions sync their conversations, memory, skills and shared attachments through Cindy's services; model providers process the requests sent to them. Provider and service billing still apply.
## Keep your favorite agents. Get a better way to work. Already using Claude Code or Codex? Cindy brings them together with **Pi**, then adds a shared interface, multi-device access, tools and a companion of your own. | Harness | What it brings | | --- | --- | | **Claude Code** | Claude Code's agent workflow, with Cindy's interface and connected tools. | | **Codex** | Codex's coding workflow, available alongside your other agents. | | **Pi** | A lean, open-source, extensible agent with support for multiple model providers. | Choose a supported harness and model combination, and change it as the work evolves. Your session stays in Cindy; switching harnesses hands off or rebuilds the engine context rather than making their internal states identical. **One agent not enough? Let her lead a team.** Use different agents for planning, parallel implementation and independent review, with a shared goal and clear acceptance criteria. ## Real work, in your actual tools Work with your files, browser and apps. Ask for a change, inspect what happened, and keep working from the result. Answers can include **charts, interactive controls and rich HTML**, not just a wall of text. Build a recurring routine with **automations**, or hand over work through connected chat channels such as Slack and Telegram. Connect more tools through **Skills, plugins and [MCP](docs/mcp-apps.md#接入)**. ## Ready from day one. Yours to shape over time. - **Create your own companions.** Give them a role, instructions, skills and recurring work — a reviewer, researcher, project partner, or something of your own. - **Make experience reusable.** Keep useful preferences and knowledge in memory; turn a good way of working into a Skill you can reuse and share. - **Extend the product.** Discover Skills and plugins in SkillHub, connect your own tools, or build on the [official plugins](https://github.com/makecindy/cindy-official-plugins). - **Help shape Cindy.** Audit the code, fork it, improve an interaction, fix a bug, or contribute a useful integration. The client is Apache-2.0 licensed. Open source means more than visible — it means changeable. [Build Cindy with us →](CONTRIBUTING.en.md) ## Start with what you already have The **client is free**. Authorize a supported subscription you already pay for, including Claude Code or Codex plans, connect your own API keys, or use a local model. You can also use Cindy's managed model service. Provider limits and billing still apply; the free client does not mean unlimited model usage. **macOS · Windows · Linux · iOS · Android** [Download Cindy](https://cindy.app/download) · [Service pricing](https://cindy.app/pricing) Linux users: see the [Ubuntu, Arch Linux and Omarchy installation guide](docs/linux.md) for installation, updates, keyring setup and migration from a manual install.
Can I set up a buddy offline, before any model inference? **Skip Sign-In** opens the desktop interface offline without a Cindy account. Cindy account-backed services require sign-in; connected third-party API models can still be used. - **Creating a named buddy needs an available model.** Choose one in **Buddies → + → New buddy**. Preparation automatically starts its first hello, before you send a message. It is marked ready when the runtime accepts that turn, not when the full reply appears. - **The built-in Cindy can be listed while waiting for a model.** During pending or failed initial preparation, name, self-introduction, personality and **What you know about me** remain read-only. Model settings stay available: use **Change Model** or retry preparation for the same buddy. - **There is no supported hand-authored declaration / zero-inference setup route**, including in Linux Global **0.1.143**, to create a named buddy, edit its profile, personality and preferences, save, and verify them after restart before any inference. - **Import is not a general declaration-text format.** Hermes / OpenClaw import can save recognized source application data before setup finishes; native packages are limited to the bundled, validated catalog. - **Compatible, available local models still infer**, including the ordinary first hello: offline is not zero-inference setup.

A few people noticed.

Every star means something.

--- ## For developers This repository contains Cindy's open-source **desktop and mobile clients** and their shared packages, organized as a pnpm monorepo. ### What's in this repo | Path | Description | | --- | --- | | `apps/desktop` | Electron desktop client | | `apps/mobile` | Expo / React Native mobile client | | `packages/*` | Shared client capabilities (auth, device-link, agent orchestration, model providers, …) | | `apps/*-bin` | Tool binaries shipped with the desktop app; none are committed — claude-code, codex, ripgrep, and pi are downloaded per platform by `pnpm install`, and the Android platform-tools binaries are fetched (pinned version, sha256-verified) before Windows packaging | **Not in this repo:** the backend service lives in a separate repository and is not part of this monorepo. | Mode | Account requirement | Availability | | --- | --- | --- | | Hosted service | Cindy cloud account | Use Cindy's full hosted service. See [pricing](https://cindy.app/pricing). | | Skip Sign-In | No Cindy sign-in required | Choose “Skip Sign-In” on the login screen to use local agents; the app then shows the account state as “Not signed in”. Server-backed capabilities are unavailable in this state. | ### Prerequisites - **Node.js** >= 22.13 (see `engines.node` in `package.json`) - **pnpm** 11.x (`>=11.25 <12`, see `engines.pnpm` and `packageManager` in `package.json`) - **Git LFS** ### Getting started Contributor setup, Git LFS, dependency updates, and access requirements are maintained in [`CONTRIBUTING.en.md`](CONTRIBUTING.en.md). Plugins are installed through SkillHub or manually. Minimal entry point: ```bash git clone https://github.com/makecindy/cindy.git cd cindy git lfs pull pnpm install ``` ### Development entry points ```bash # Mainland China Cindy account pnpm restart:desktop:remote --region=cn # Global Cindy account pnpm restart:desktop:remote --region=global ``` Remote development uses your own Cindy cloud account and existing login state, so you can continue existing sessions and work while developing the client. Use `cn` for Mainland China accounts and `global` for everyone else; do not rely on the internal default. Full desktop, mobile, data-isolation, and validation workflows are in [`CONTRIBUTING.en.md`](CONTRIBUTING.en.md). “Skip Sign-In” on the login screen runs local agents without a Cindy account (shown in the app as “Not signed in”), not a connection to a local server. Server-backed capabilities are unavailable in this state. **About the default servers:** the client connects to Cindy's official cloud services by default (endpoint manifests in [`config/endpoint.json`](config/endpoint.json) and [`config/endpoint.global.json`](config/endpoint.global.json); desktop auto-updates also come from the official CDN). This is intentional — external developers don't need to self-host a server: sign in with your own Cindy account in a dev build and develop / test directly against the official servers. Skill Hub migration uses two separate manifest fields: released clients keep using `skillhubApiBaseUrl` (the deprecated XD proxy), while current clients use `cindySkillHubApiBaseUrl`. The current client deliberately does not fall back to the legacy field when the new endpoint is absent. ### Architecture - [`DESIGN.md`](DESIGN.md) — visual design system, color tokens, and UI conventions - [`docs/README.md`](docs/README.md) — complete documentation and rules index - [`docs/auth-realm-routing.md`](docs/auth-realm-routing.md) — organization SSO region discovery and session endpoint routing - [`CONTRIBUTING.en.md`](CONTRIBUTING.en.md) — contributor setup, validation, and submission workflow - [`AGENTS.md`](AGENTS.md) — engineering rules, launch/runtime contracts, and module boundaries - [`docs/dev-rules/`](docs/dev-rules/) — deep-dive architecture docs (e.g. Orca multi-agent orchestration) ## Contributing Contributions go through pull requests into `main`. Read [`CONTRIBUTING.en.md`](CONTRIBUTING.en.md) first, then use [`.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md`](.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md). Every commit needs a [Developer Certificate of Origin](DCO) sign-off (`git commit -s`); a DCO check on each pull request enforces it, and no CLA is required. English · 简体中文

Download Cindy  ·  Website  ·  Build with us  ·  Get help

★ GitHub Trending #1 · 2026.10.26

Cindy is an open-source AI agent, ready out of the box and yours to shape. Connect your computers and phone, bring the models and subscriptions you already use, and build a companion that knows how you like to work.

All your devices. One Cindy.

Your work computer, home desktop, laptop and phone belong together.

  • Pick up the same work. Open a session from another device, continue the conversation, and access its files without copying everything into a new chat.
  • Share more than a screen. Use model providers configured on another computer — including supported subscriptions, API providers and local models.
  • Reach your whole desktop. Built-in remote desktop on your phone lets you open apps, type and operate a connected computer when a chat isn't enough.

Your computer becomes your server: no server rental or self-hosting setup.

How connections and data work

For remote access to your computers, keep them online, sign in with the same account and enable the relevant permissions. Model sharing requires allowing remote access to that provider; remote desktop also needs its own permissions. Project files stay on their computer — remote access is not whole-disk sync. Cloud companions sync their conversations, memory, skills and shared attachments through Cindy's services; model providers process the requests sent to them. Provider and service billing still apply.

Keep your favorite agents. Get a better way to work.

Already using Claude Code or Codex? Cindy brings them together with Pi, then adds a shared interface, multi-device access, tools and a companion of your own.

Harness What it brings
Claude Code Claude Code's agent workflow, with Cindy's interface and connected tools.
Codex Codex's coding workflow, available alongside your other agents.
Pi A lean, open-source, extensible agent with support for multiple model providers.

Choose a supported harness and model combination, and change it as the work evolves. Your session stays in Cindy; switching harnesses hands off or rebuilds the engine context rather than making their internal states identical.

One agent not enough? Let her lead a team. Use different agents for planning, parallel implementation and independent review, with a shared goal and clear acceptance criteria.

Real work, in your actual tools

Work with your files, browser and apps. Ask for a change, inspect what happened, and keep working from the result. Answers can include charts, interactive controls and rich HTML, not just a wall of text.

Build a recurring routine with automations, or hand over work through connected chat channels such as Slack and Telegram. Connect more tools through Skills, plugins and MCP.

Ready from day one. Yours to shape over time.

  • Create your own companions. Give them a role, instructions, skills and recurring work — a reviewer, researcher, project partner, or something of your own.
  • Make experience reusable. Keep useful preferences and knowledge in memory; turn a good way of working into a Skill you can reuse and share.
  • Extend the product. Discover Skills and plugins in SkillHub, connect your own tools, or build on the official plugins.
  • Help shape Cindy. Audit the code, fork it, improve an interaction, fix a bug, or contribute a useful integration. The client is Apache-2.0 licensed.

Open source means more than visible — it means changeable. Build Cindy with us →

Start with what you already have

The client is free. Authorize a supported subscription you already pay for, including Claude Code or Codex plans, connect your own API keys, or use a local model. You can also use Cindy's managed model service. Provider limits and billing still apply; the free client does not mean unlimited model usage.

macOS · Windows · Linux · iOS · Android

Download Cindy · Service pricing

Linux users: see the Ubuntu, Arch Linux and Omarchy installation guide for installation, updates, keyring setup and migration from a manual install.

Can I set up a buddy offline, before any model inference?

Skip Sign-In opens the desktop interface offline without a Cindy account. Cindy account-backed services require sign-in; connected third-party API models can still be used.

  • Creating a named buddy needs an available model. Choose one in Buddies → + → New buddy. Preparation automatically starts its first hello, before you send a message. It is marked ready when the runtime accepts that turn, not when the full reply appears.
  • The built-in Cindy can be listed while waiting for a model. During pending or failed initial preparation, name, self-introduction, personality and What you know about me remain read-only. Model settings stay available: use Change Model or retry preparation for the same buddy.
  • There is no supported hand-authored declaration / zero-inference setup route, including in Linux Global 0.1.143, to create a named buddy, edit its profile, personality and preferences, save, and verify them after restart before any inference.
  • Import is not a general declaration-text format. Hermes / OpenClaw import can save recognized source application data before setup finishes; native packages are limited to the bundled, validated catalog.
  • Compatible, available local models still infer, including the ordinary first hello: offline is not zero-inference setup.

A few people noticed.

Every star means something.

For developers

This repository contains Cindy's open-source desktop and mobile clients and their shared packages, organized as a pnpm monorepo.

What's in this repo

Path Description
apps/desktop Electron desktop client
apps/mobile Expo / React Native mobile client
packages/* Shared client capabilities (auth, device-link, agent orchestration, model providers, …)
apps/*-bin Tool binaries shipped with the desktop app; none are committed — claude-code, codex, ripgrep, and pi are downloaded per platform by pnpm install, and the Android platform-tools binaries are fetched (pinned version, sha256-verified) before Windows packaging

Not in this repo: the backend service lives in a separate repository and is not part of this monorepo.

Mode Account requirement Availability
Hosted service Cindy cloud account Use Cindy's full hosted service. See pricing.
Skip Sign-In No Cindy sign-in required Choose “Skip Sign-In” on the login screen to use local agents; the app then shows the account state as “Not signed in”. Server-backed capabilities are unavailable in this state.

Prerequisites

  • Node.js >= 22.13 (see engines.node in package.json)
  • pnpm 11.x (>=11.25 <12, see engines.pnpm and packageManager in package.json)
  • Git LFS

Getting started

Contributor setup, Git LFS, dependency updates, and access requirements are maintained in CONTRIBUTING.en.md. Plugins are installed through SkillHub or manually.

Minimal entry point:

git clone https://github.com/makecindy/cindy.git
cd cindy
git lfs pull
pnpm install

Development entry points

# Mainland China Cindy account
pnpm restart:desktop:remote --region=cn

# Global Cindy account
pnpm restart:desktop:remote --region=global

Remote development uses your own Cindy cloud account and existing login state, so you can continue existing sessions and work while developing the client. Use cn for Mainland China accounts and global for everyone else; do not rely on the internal default. Full desktop, mobile, data-isolation, and validation workflows are in CONTRIBUTING.en.md.

“Skip Sign-In” on the login screen runs local agents without a Cindy account (shown in the app as “Not signed in”), not a connection to a local server. Server-backed capabilities are unavailable in this state.

About the default servers: the client connects to Cindy's official cloud services by default (endpoint manifests in config/endpoint.json and config/endpoint.global.json; desktop auto-updates also come from the official CDN). This is intentional — external developers don't need to self-host a server: sign in with your own Cindy account in a dev build and develop / test directly against the official servers.

Skill Hub migration uses two separate manifest fields: released clients keep using skillhubApiBaseUrl (the deprecated XD proxy), while current clients use cindySkillHubApiBaseUrl. The current client deliberately does not fall back to the legacy field when the new endpoint is absent.

Architecture

  • DESIGN.md — visual design system, color tokens, and UI conventions
  • docs/README.md — complete documentation and rules index
  • docs/auth-realm-routing.md — organization SSO region discovery and session endpoint routing
  • CONTRIBUTING.en.md — contributor setup, validation, and submission workflow
  • AGENTS.md — engineering rules, launch/runtime contracts, and module boundaries
  • docs/dev-rules/ — deep-dive architecture docs (e.g. Orca multi-agent orchestration)

Contributing

Contributions go through pull requests into main. Read CONTRIBUTING.en.md first, then use .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md. Every commit needs a Developer Certificate of Origin sign-off (git commit -s); a DCO check on each pull request enforces it, and no CLA is required. Please also follow CODE_OF_CONDUCT.en.md. For ordinary usage questions, see SUPPORT.en.md; report security issues privately through SECURITY.en.md.

Security

Never commit credentials or authorization files to the working tree. If you discover a security issue, follow SECURITY.en.md to report it privately rather than opening a public issue.

Privacy & telemetry

Official distribution builds include TapDB usage analytics for app launches and return visits, including a device identifier and OS / app version. After sign-in, visits use a regional account alias. The same alias links daily model choices and token totals from participating desktop devices. Payment statistics use a separate alias. Desktop uses a fresh device identifier. On mobile, someone with older records may be able to link the new alias to the original account ID through the existing device identifier. These statistics exclude chats, prompts, files and working-directory data.

You can disable usage analytics without editing code: on Desktop, use Settings → About → Usage statistics; on Mobile, use Usage statistics in Settings. The SDK checks the stored privacy-consent state and the statistics preference, which defaults to on. Accepting the Privacy Policy records consent; a one-time migration also records consent for eligible existing signed-in users. Upgrading keeps the current setting. Per-account model usage starts at upgrade and enrollment on each desktop. Earlier usage is not uploaded as account history.

Known Mobile exception: enterprise SSO skips the policy-acceptance step. If no analytics consent record exists and that sign-in is restored after restarting the app, the current migration can mark even a new installation as consented. With TapDB configured and statistics enabled, reporting can then start without explicit policy acceptance. See Mobile sign-in restoration and the consent migration. Turning off Usage statistics prevents reporting from being enabled by this migration.

  • Desktop stops subsequent analytics reporting immediately when disabled. Local mode (Skip sign-in) does not report to TapDB.
  • Mobile immediately unlinks the account and stops reports explicitly triggered by Cindy. An already initialized native SDK cannot be uninitialized; fully quit and relaunch the app to keep the SDK uninitialized.

Implementation: Desktop consent and settings, Desktop SDK, Mobile consent, and Mobile SDK.

Online heartbeats and diagnostic logs are separate mechanisms, unaffected by the usage statistics switch. Desktop sends heartbeats to Cindy services only during a verified cloud sign-in (account ID, platform, and version); local mode sends none. Desktop native crash dumps stay local and are never uploaded automatically. Diagnostic logs can be uploaded manually; a separate, default-off automatic crash log upload option is also available. Log uploads require privacy consent. See the heartbeat implementation and log upload rules.

Building from source? You are not required to keep analytics:

  • Desktop development builds do not initialize TapDB by default. Explicitly setting XDT_TAPDB_DEV=1 lifts the build gate but still requires consent and the statistics preference. Self-packaged Desktop builds use the same analytics gates as official builds; you can disable analytics in Settings.
  • Mobile does not initialize the SDK without injected TapDB configuration (clientId / clientToken). This does not mean all source builds default to off: the self-hosted release pipeline requires nonempty configuration, while local development permits empty values. See the Mobile build guide.

License / 许可证

Except as otherwise noted, the source code in this repository is licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0. Individual source files do not carry per-file license headers; the repository-root LICENSE governs.

Model weights, datasets, prompts, trademarks, and other separately identified materials may be subject to their own license terms and are not automatically covered by the repository-level Apache-2.0 grant. Third-party open-source components retain their own copyright and license. Their attribution notices and SPDX SBOMs are managed under docs/legal/, with artifact-specific outputs in docs/legal/notices/. See NOTICE for this project's copyright and attribution information.

releases.name: v0.1.149-beta
releases.body:
Desktop release 0.1.149

## 更新说明
### 🧠 智能路由与模型供应商
模型组已并入模型供应商，可以把多个供应商组合成智能路由并按需自动切换；新增混合 OpenAI 订阅与 API Key 账号池、自定义连接名称与图标，并可直接接入已有的命令行订阅登录。

### 🧩 插件引擎更完整
插件引擎任务现在支持分叉、侧聊、/learn、目标模式和自动起名，也能在工作区、个人 IM 渠道与伙伴中运行；插件下载不再要求预先声明大小，安装更少被限流阻断。

### 🌐 Agent-Net 更稳更快
桌面端 Agent-Net 改用原生引擎，直连与中转会自动选路并改善跨区域连接与端口设置；旧的设备直连供应商分享会无感迁移到 Agent-Net。

### 🖥️ 远程桌面控制增强
GNOME Wayland 主机可用本机鼠标远程控制，X11 主机也改用本机光标；中文等非 ASCII 文字通过剪贴板输入并恢复原剪贴板，被控提示只在桌面浮窗显示、不会出现在远程画面里。

### 🗂️ 伙伴工作区迁移
新增伙伴工作区迁移能力，可预检、登记、查看进度和取消，并在启动前完成迁移、保留可恢复副本；支持重复迁移、搬回默认位置，并新增默认目录设置和冷启动进度页。

### 💬 群聊与消息体验
群聊里可以点名自己，并支持右键在独立窗口打开；云端建群更简单并在首次进群时展开邀请，回复他人时会引用对应消息；群通知选择会被保存，移动端也能经电脑管理群里的 Cindy。

### 📱 移动端体验
移动端完善了音频播放，解决 iOS 预加载卡死并让音频卡随内容伸缩；项目设置移入左滑操作，侧边追问创建期间即可输入和排队发送，iOS 编辑 MCP App 小字段不再被遮挡。

### 🗓️ 自动化与定时任务
自动化表单支持自定义 Cron；插件引擎任务可在已完成的自动化上继续，切换引擎失败时会阻止发送；定时任务在换机关闭旧会话后仍能恢复，插件更新后前置检查脚本也能找到模块。

### 💼 任务体验
侧边追问打开更快、创建期间即可输入；新建任务会沿用上次的权限模式，复制任务链接的快捷键可自定义，任务可在项目间移动，逐模型自动压缩阈值改为滑杆调节。

### 📄 文件审查与预览
文件预览浮层不再随工具行重建而消失，文件被改动时会提示更新；共享访客可只读查看整仓当前 Git 差异，聊天里的 PR/MR 链接悬停即可看到详情，分享消息时的勾选与全选按钮也恢复正常。

### 👤 账号、登录与稳定性
设置页支持换绑登录手机号或邮箱，登录凭据库异常时可重新登录直接恢复。macOS 正式包签名与公证已修复，Pi 与 Codex 的限流、超时和内存问题更可控，设备连接与 Linux 无人值守更新更稳。

Desktop release 0.1.148

## 更新说明
### 🔑 OpenAI 账号池可合并使用
OpenAI 订阅和官方 API Key 可以并入同一个账号池，系统按模型、额度和可用性自动选号；某个账号额度用完或鉴权失败时，同一会话会交给备用账号继续，设置里可调整顺序、权重与并发上限。 @fmfsaisai

### ⚡ 共享模型运行更省资源
把模型分享给其他设备时，主机不再反复核对同一份配置，也不会为每条用量记录整份重写账本；用量会先在内存中合并，并在退出前统一保存。 @yan-xdt

releases.name: v0.1.147-beta

Desktop release 0.1.147

## 更新说明
### 🧩 插件市场焕新
插件管理与市场重新设计，首次打开和详情读取更快；可以在对话中直接安装并使用插件，安装确认默认展示全部权限，远程插件页出错后也能恢复。 @DavidShenXD @FicoHub @GaoWeiLiuXD @nanaco666

### 🔌 插件能力增强
插件登录新增设备码方式，不用跳回浏览器也能完成授权；任务里可以用 / 调用 Cindy 技能，插件任务结果会自动回传到发起它的 IM 对话；空闲的插件任务引擎会在 30 分钟后自动释放。 @MagicLizi @dashhuang

### 🖼️ 任务图片可跨轮翻看
在任务里点开任意图片后，可以用上一张 / 下一张（或 ←/→）在该任务加载过的全部图片间翻看，不再局限于同一条消息；重复图片、工具产出和插件卡片里的图也能正确归类。 @DavidShenXD @billythegod @xuzini-xzn @yan-xdt

### 📡 多设备与远程连接更稳
弱网、慢中转和断网时，手机与电脑之间不再轻易误判断线，连接会按需重连并自动恢复；手机断网或锁屏后保留登录状态，消息不会重复或丢失。 @MagicLizi @amanayayatu-tech @billythegod @dashhuang @yan-xdt

### 🐋 任务与自动化更可靠
Orca 多 Agent 任务在接管、停止、续跑和恢复时更可靠，晚到的确认不会覆盖你手动做出的选择；一次性自动化遇到忙碌任务会排队等待，绑定插件引擎任务的自动化也能正常续发。 @DavidShenXD @FicoHub @MagicLizi @amanayayatu-tech @dashhuang @xuzini-xzn @yan-xdt

### 📷 截图读码更可靠
需要你扫二维码或读短信验证码时，Cindy 能识别缩成一像素的验证码框，等待期间不会把登录窗口反复拉到前台；文件不在当前电脑上时会直接说明，不再含糊提示。

### 🤖 模型、Codex 与用量
Codex 的 Fast 与 Ultrafast 模式覆盖更多官方 OpenAI 模型，切换模型或服务繁忙时的恢复更稳妥。用量统计不再重复记账，切换登录方式或凭证后账号数据也会重新核对。 @DavidShenXD @FicoHub @amanayayatu-tech @dashhuang @xuzini-xzn @yan-xdt

### ✨ 界面、群聊与手机端
侧栏状态点对齐、悬停时操作按钮原地替换；群聊显示企业实名、部门与外部标识，伙伴头像扩到 26 个。手机端修复图片闪白、视频预览滚动与键盘拖拽后的跟随，导入新版 DeepSeek 历史记录也更稳定。 @DavidShenXD @amanayayatu-t

releases.name: v0.1.146
releases.body:
Desktop release 0.1.146

## 更新说明
### 🤖 模型组自动换来源更聪明
出错时自动换来源现在按报错类型处理：来源本身的问题立刻切换，临时故障先在同一来源重试两次。设置页可按每个模式单独开关，续跑时会写明从哪个来源换到哪个、为什么。 @amanayayatu-tech @nanaco666 @xuzini-xzn @yan-xdt @zqchris

### 🧩 插件引擎与插件市场
官方模型插件可直接在供应商选择器里看到并配置，Antigravity 等插件模型有了高级设置，供应商菜单新增卸载入口；插件可显示任务进度、在指定电脑打开会话或文件类型，市场图标与安装来源说明也更稳。 @GaoWeiLiuXD @MagicLizi @amanayayatu-tech @dashhuang @nanaco666 @xuzini-xzn @zqchris

### 🎙️ 伙伴实时语音通话
伙伴现在可以用 OpenAI 或百炼的自己的密钥（BYOK）进行实时语音通话。 @horizon554

### 💬 伙伴 IM 与消息更顺
伙伴 IM 连接改为并行启动，Telegram 握手限时 15 秒，超时保留输入并提示重试；首次连接显示「连接中」，不再误判主力电脑离线。iMessage 忙时消息可补进当前轮，飞书引用与 MR 跟进更完整。 @DavidShenXD @amanayayatu-tech @dashhuang @elfcv @nanaco666 @xuzini-xzn @zqchris

### 🦾 任务与多 Agent 更可靠
已启动任务旁显示实时状态；Orca 的 Lead、Worker 支持模型组，Worker 从最新 main 启动并保留本地分支，失败可手动继续。发送前检查与运行中删消息会说明原因和重试方式，跨设备可恢复工作树。 @DavidShenXD @StarDuster @amanayayatu-tech @dashhuang @elfcv @xuzini-xzn @yan-xdt

### 📱 手机端更顺手
大屏竖屏任务页改用单个悬浮列表按钮，任务内下钻的返回导航统一了，从消息链接打开任务后右滑可回原任务。短暂切后台不断开局域网连接，聊天里的 MCP 应用保持存活，Android 图片保存保留原格式。 @DavidShenXD @amanayayatu-tech @dashhuang @zqchris

### 🖥️ 桌面体验与 Windows 打磨
外观设置新增宽屏聊天宽度滑杆，低档逐级生效，对话布局术语统一并可恢复默认。Agent 导出任务可存到固定目录，Windows 托盘卡片新增开关，HDR 截图不再偏亮，项目选择器支持方向键与回车。 @DavidShenXD @MagicLizi @amana

releases.name: v0.1.145
releases.body:
Desktop release 0.1.145

## 更新说明
### 🧠 模型组自动接替
定时任务和自动化能选模型组，每次运行前按设定重新挑选来源；新增用完再换、余量最多的先用、按权重三种选法，配额用完时会在组内自动接替。 @zqchris

### 🧩 插件引擎多账号与用量
插件引擎供应商支持多账号，可设置分配方式、并发、权重和任务绑定，发送前自动换号；菜单栏、小组件和模型选择器能直接看到剩余配额。 @MagicLizi @xuzini-xzn @zqchris

### 🧰 插件市场与表单
插件市场重新整理了分类、更新按钮和来源标签；插件现在能请 Cindy 弹出标准表单收集设置，并支持具名工具挂载和预览页签复用。 @GaoWeiLiuXD @MagicLizi

### ⚡ 连接、设备与远程控制
设备连接新增智能直连/中继选路和双延迟显示；被移除的设备可在本机直接重新加入，两台电脑共用同一身份时会提示换新身份；远程控制独立主机时的发消息与模型设置也补齐了。 @MagicLizi @StarDuster @dashhuang

### 💬 官方 IM 机器人与消息
官方 IM 机器人新增 Discord，私信或执行 /bind 即可关联；飞书支持按群单独设置；iMessage 能把原图和大附件交给模型并按需取回，HEIC 预览和定时任务结果投递也更可靠。 @MagicLizi @xd-bobo @zqchris

### 📊 模型、用量与账号
ChatGPT 套餐用完会先换到还有配额的账号，没得换才动用 credits；菜单栏能看智谱 GLM Coding Plan 余量，供应商计费更准确；新增 Token Rhythm 连接预设，独立订阅的图片生成恢复可用。 @MagicLizi @StarDuster @WZBbiao @dashhuang @jjaychen1e @joei4cm @xuzini-xzn @zqchris @zyjisdog

### 🤝 伙伴与任务体验
伙伴在私聊、群聊、话题等每个场景都按普通项目任务运行，能力保持一致，也能为自己选择插件引擎模型；辅助模型全部不可用时会明确提示；锁屏或无人确认的超时提示会讲清原因，不再被误当成拒绝。 @dashhuang @elfcv @zqchris

### 📱 手机端更顺手
手机端删掉工作目录后会自动回收对应的预览服务；灵动岛和锁屏的实时活动不再显示「过期」画面，到期后照常显示直到被结束；模型选择器在分享暂时读不到时也会保留条目。 @dashhuang @zqchris

### 🛡️ 稳定性、细节与协议
退出时的崩溃会被完整记录，反复点退出也不会卡住清理；MCP 卡片切换不再闪白，截图与导出颜色更准确，自定义地址带 /v1 时不再拼出重复路径；个人账号在协议更新后需先确

aiSummary.oneLiner: An open-source, local AI agent that uses real files and logged-in applications to perform out-of-the-box tasks.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Cindy operates as a comprehensive AI agent that runs entirely locally on your own machine. It seamlessly integrates multiple harnesses, models, and tools into a single desktop experience capable of interacting with your real files and authenticated applications. Initial support includes Claude Code and Codex harnesses, with a native harness under active development. The platform allows models and harnesses to mix freely, switching mid-task depending on the workspace requirements. It connects to Cindy's official cloud services for telemetry and auto-updates while retaining local execution capabilities.
keyFeatures: Local execution: Run the AI agent directly on your machine accessing local files and authenticated apps.
Multiple harnesses: Support for Claude Code and Codex harnesses with seamless mid-task switching.
Cloud integration: Connect to official Cindy cloud services for updates while optionally running in local mode.
Skill Hub migration: Support advanced endpoints using the new cindySkillHubApiBaseUrl manifest field.
Analytics control: Allow building from source without TapDB telemetry by stripping specific initialization calls.

useCases.title: Automating desktop workflows
useCases.description: Interact directly with locally authenticated applications to accomplish daily tasks.

useCases.title: Developing locally
useCases.description: Build and test client features remotely using official cloud servers without self-hosting.

useCases.title: Switching models mid-task
useCases.description: Leverage Claude Code for text parsing and switch to Codex for script generation seamlessly.

useCases.title: Running without cloud login
useCases.description: Execute local agents in 'Skip Sign-In' mode for completely isolated operations.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: This agent is designed for developers and power users wanting deep local integration for automated tasks. Prerequisites include Node.js 22.x, pnpm 10.x, and Git LFS for source compilation, requiring a modern desktop environment.
aiSummary.gettingStarted: git clone https://github.com/makecindy/cindy.git && cd cindy && git lfs pull && pnpm install
